subject.title: refactor(sdk): collapse plan updates to typed steps

question: May the next OpenClaw release intentionally change the shipped `onPlanUpdate.steps` value from `string[]` to `AgentPlanStep[]` without a deprecation window?
rationale: The implementation is internally coherent, but deciding whether to break a released third-party plugin callback is a compatibility and release-policy choice that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Preserve the deprecation window
options.body: Keep released string `steps` alongside typed `planSteps`, migrate bundled consumers, and schedule removal through the documented compatibility process.

options.title: Approve a versioned break
options.body: Land the typed-only contract only with explicit major-version approval, migration documentation, external upgrade proof, and release-note context.

options.title: Pause for consumer evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers establish whether any external channel plugins consume the released string field and choose the permanent contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve the deprecation window
recommendation.body: Keep released string `steps` alongside typed `planSteps`, migrate bundled consumers, and schedule removal through the documented compatibility process.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR identifies an owner decision and is self-assigned to the contributor carrying the cross-channel SDK change.
